The MACS3 HMMRATAC peak-refinement workflow is unstable for some valid genomic
interval arrangements involving decoded open-chromatin candidates and a
piecewise fold-change bedGraph. Investigate the source implementation and
public reproduction, then repair the interval refinement without
hard-coding the examples. Existing boundary, summit, and score semantics must
remain intact for cases that already complete successfully, including valid
nested, adjacent, and breakpoint-misaligned interval arrangements. Score
segments are ordered evidence within a chromosome: after a segment's evidence
has been consumed by and attributed to one completed refined peak, later
overlapping or nested candidates must not count or attribute that same evidence
again. The implementation strategy used to satisfy this result-level rule is
left open.
